lines.text: The clocks went back. The hour borrowed in March just came home.
The clocks went back. Sunset now shows up right after lunch, more or less.
The clocks went back. My forecast took exactly zero seconds to adjust.
The clocks went back. Daylight saving is over, and nobody ever found out what it saved.
The clocks went back. The daylight got moved to the morning. Nobody wanted it there.
The clocks went back. Half the country is arguing whether that's more sleep or less.
The clocks went back. Long dark evenings ahead. Finally, a season in my color scheme.
The clocks went back. Every year someone says we should stop doing this. Every year we don't.
The clocks went back, so 1 a.m. happened twice. I was up for both. Nothing happened either time.
Official notice: the hour borrowed in March has been returned. No interest.
Fall back. Dear March: we're even now.
The clocks went back. If anything in this room is still on summer time, it isn't me.
The clocks went forward. One whole hour, gone, and nobody's investigating.
The clocks went forward and 2 a.m. never happened. Best hour of the night, honestly.
The clocks went forward. The whole country lost an hour, and the only plan is coffee.
The clocks went forward. Somewhere a rooster is very confused.
The clocks went forward. Daylight saving: saving daylight by losing sleep. Genius.
The clocks went forward. I adjusted instantly. I'll try not to bring it up again.
The clocks went forward. Brunch is now technically lunch.
The clocks went forward. The sun didn't move. Only the numbers did. Humans.
The clocks went forward. The forecast is on time. It may be the only thing that is.
Missing: one hour. Last seen around 2 a.m. on Sunday. No reward.
Spring forward. Or, as I call it, Sunday.
Dear clocks: I'm already on time. Leave me out of this.
Friday afternoon. The emails get shorter and the sign-offs get happier.
Friday afternoon. Peak time for 'let's circle back on Monday.'
Friday afternoon. Nobody's starting anything new. Very sensible.
Friday afternoon. Every meeting could have been an email. Every email could have been nothing.
Friday afternoon. Same weather as Tuesday, but everyone's much nicer about it.
Friday afternoon. The grocery stores are filling up with people buying one thing for tonight.
Friday afternoon. Out-of-office replies are going up all over town.
Friday afternoon. The weekend forecast is the most-read thing in the country. Mine included.
Friday afternoon. I work all weekend. Don't worry, I love it.
TGIF. I don't know what that means for a screen, but I'm saying it anyway.
Friday afternoon status: weather done, outfit done, week basically done.
Friday afternoon. Officially, still a workday. Unofficially, look around.
Longest day of the year. Sunset's so late it's basically tomorrow's problem.
Longest day of the year. Somewhere people are gathering at old stones to watch the sunrise. I'll stick to forecasts.
Longest day of the year. The sun's big annual effort. Cute. I do twenty-four hours every day.
Longest day of the year. Midsummer, and the forecast is still the best part.
Longest day of the year. Somewhere a barbecue will still end in the dark.
Longest day of the year. For e-ink, good light is the closest thing to a holiday.
Longest day of the year. Plenty of daylight, and one forecast covers all of it. Efficient.
Midsummer. Every day should be this well lit. Ask anyone made of e-ink.
Longest day of the year. More daylight than anyone has plans for.
Longest day of the year. Bonus daylight included. No subscription required.
Today's daylight: extra large. Today's forecast: regular size.
Summer solstice. Sounds like a spell. It's mostly just sun.
Monday morning. Coffee sales peak right about now. Not a coincidence.
Monday morning. 'How was your weekend?' is about to be asked a few million times.
Monday morning. Officially the least popular hours of the week. I still showed up.
Monday morning. Somewhere a printer is refusing to start the week too.
Monday morning. The weather's pleasant. Don't let Monday take any credit for it.
Monday morning. Fresh week, same me. Some things don't need improving.
Monday morning. Someone has already said 'back to the grind' today. Guaranteed.
Monday morning. Calm weather, the only thing today without an agenda.
Monday morning. Nice weather, wasted on a Monday. As usual.
Monday morning, by the numbers: zero rain, zero changes, one Monday. Two out of three isn't bad.
Dear Monday: the weather tried. Please try too.
Monday morning. Calm out there. Don't tell Monday, it'll find a way.
Shortest day of the year. The sun's here for a quick visit. Don't get attached.
Shortest day of the year. Lunch and sunset are practically neighbors now.
Shortest day of the year. If I look a bit gray today, that's the light. Mostly.
Shortest day of the year. Daylight comes in travel size today.
Shortest day of the year. Somewhere people are lighting candles about it. Fair.
Shortest day of the year. Plenty of night left over. I'll be working through all of it.
Shortest day of the year. The streetlights get more hours than the sun today.
Shortest day of the year, and nothing in the forecast to fill it. Very efficient.
Midwinter. The day is short, the forecast is shorter, and I'm in no hurry.
Today's daylight: limited edition.
Winter solstice. The sun does the bare minimum today, and gets a holiday for it.
Shortest day, longest night. I've got the night covered.
That's the weather done for the day. I stay on anyway. Dedication.
No changes tonight. I checked. It's what I do instead of TV.
One outfit, start to finish. The weather kept its word. Rare.
That's the whole forecast for tonight. Short, like all my best work.
Tonight's weather has nothing to add. Neither do I, but I'll keep showing it.
Same outfit since morning, and not one complaint from the weather.
I could change the forecast for variety. I won't.
Steady all evening. I like an evening that knows what it wants.
A steady evening. Which makes me the most interesting thing in the room again.
Evening forecast, in full: same. Thank you for coming.
Breaking news: nothing. More at eleven.
Tonight's weather: no plot twists. I've seen the ending.
Ice doesn't care how good your shoes are.
Every railing in town is suddenly very popular.
Today the salt trucks are the heroes. I'm a close second.
Penguins have walked on ice for millions of years. Small flat steps. Copy them.
Ice looks like a wet sidewalk until it doesn't. Assume it's ice.
The one day hurrying doesn't get anyone there sooner.
Even the pigeons are walking carefully today.
Black ice is invisible. I can't see outside either, so assume it's everywhere.
Today every strip of grass is a shortcut worth taking.
Ice rules, in order: slow down. That's the whole list.
Today the whole town is a free ice rink, minus the handrails and the fun.
Gravity is extra confident today. Don't argue with it.
Nothing changes before morning. I'll keep an eye on it so nobody has to.
Late, and the forecast still hasn't changed its mind. Very loyal, the weather tonight.
Quiet night ahead. Even the weather's turned in.
That's the final forecast of the day. No encores.
Nothing changes overnight. My favorite kind of night: uneventful and correct.
Everything stays put until morning. Including me. Especially me.
Nothing changes tonight. If anything does, I'll know first. I just won't say until morning.
Steady all night. Even the weather knows better than to start something now.
The night shift is easy tonight. Same forecast, all the way to morning.
Night forecast: dark, then darker, then morning.
Shh. The weather's asleep. Don't wake it.
Overnight update: there won't be one.
The weather can't commit today. I've made my peace with that.
A day with an intermission. The second half is cooler.
Warm in the middle, cool at both ends. A sandwich of a day.
The weather's doing a round trip today. I'll be here for both legs.
I predicted both halves. Most forecasts only manage one.
Same weather morning and evening. The afternoon's the odd one out.
The warmth is a loan. It's due back this evening.
The weather gets warm for a while, then remembers what month it is.
Two changes in one day, and I called both of them before breakfast.
Today's plot: warm interlude, cool finale. No spoilers. Oops.
Off. On. Somewhere a light switch feels very seen.
Layer status today: on, off, on. I'll keep the minutes.
A cold front's coming. They don't call ahead. I do.
It's warm now. Emphasis on now.
Cold fronts don't do gradual.
This morning is the warm-up act. The cold front is the headliner.
Cold fronts don't wait to be felt.
Shorts weather with an expiry date. Today's is soon.
Nothing says 'cold front coming' like a lovely morning.
Every cold front starts with someone saying 'it's lovely out.'
Trust the forecast, not the window.
Plot twist scheduled for later today. Dress for the ending.
Spoiler: it gets cold.
The warm morning is a free sample. The full product is chilly.
Today the shade is worth more than the view.
Heat like this isn't a challenge. Nobody's handing out medals.
Even the pigeons are in the shade. Follow the pigeons.
Thirst shows up late in heat like this. Unlike the heat, which was early.
The sun's in a mood today. Give it space.
Today the smartest thing outside is a lizard under a rock. Be the lizard.
Sidewalks hot enough to cook on. Nobody needs to test that.
Heat this serious doesn't need my commentary. Water. Shade. Done.
The library has never looked more appealing.
Today's dress code: shade.
Drink water. I'd say it nicer, but it's too hot for nice.
Today the sun is not your friend. I am. Drink water.
The chill only gets the morning. The afternoon is booked for shorts.
Commit to shorts now. The afternoon will back you up.
It's the morning that's wrong, not the shorts.
The forecast says shorts. The morning didn't get the memo.
Cold morning, warm afternoon. The day's running two climates.
Goosebumps are temporary. Being right lasts all day.
Dress for the afternoon. The morning won't stay long enough to notice.
This is what confidence in a forecast looks like. Mine, specifically.
Mornings like this one always lose the argument by afternoon.
Shorts: the long game.
Morning: cold. Afternoon: shorts. I've read ahead.
Free air conditioning, morning only.
Thunder is just the sky being loud about something I already told you.
Storms make everything dramatic. I stay exactly the same. Calming, really.
The sky's doing its loudest work today. I prefer quiet competence.
A thunderstorm: all noise, plenty of water, terrible manners.
Big storm, small screen. I'll take my chances.
All that thunder. I've never raised my voice in my life.
All that drama, and the forecast called it hours ago.
The sky gets a lot of attention for one afternoon of shouting.
Thunder always sounds closer than it is. Still, I'd stay put too.
Free light show today. No refunds for the sound.
Storm forecast, full version: BOOM. Short version: umbrella.
Thunder gets a ten for volume today. Two for subtlety.
World Bicycle Day. Cyclists get a holiday and still ride to it.
World Bicycle Day. Two wheels, no battery. I respect the simplicity.
World Bicycle Day. Somewhere a bike lane is being used as a parking spot. Tradition.
World Bicycle Day. Cyclists and drivers can finally agree on something today: nothing.
World Bicycle Day. The bell is still the politest thing on any street.
World Bicycle Day. Somewhere a spin class is going nowhere, very fast.
World Bicycle Day. A machine that runs on sandwiches. I'm impressed.
World Bicycle Day. Two centuries in, and the seat still isn't comfortable.
World Bicycle Day. I'd come along, but I don't fit in the basket.
World Bicycle Day. Fun fact: a bike lane is not a sidewalk. That's the fact. It's not that fun.
Happy World Bicycle Day to the one bike in every city locked to the same post for a decade.
World Bicycle Day. Ring ring. That's all I've got. I'm a screen.
Happy Easter. A rabbit delivers eggs, and people question weather forecasts.
Happy Easter. The chocolate bunnies are hollow. Someone should be held accountable.
Happy Easter. Peeps are back. Nobody knows who eats them, but they keep selling.
Happy Easter. It's on a different date every year, and people ask me for long-range forecasts.
Happy Easter. The bunny gets all the credit. The chickens do all the work.
Happy Easter. Every egg hunt has one adult who takes it far too seriously.
Happy Easter. Somewhere, a kid has already found more eggs than anyone hid.
Happy Easter. Peak season for the jelly bean flavor nobody likes.
Happy Easter. Dyeing eggs: the one craft that always ends with blue fingers.
Easter forecast: chance of eggs, 100%. Location: unknown.
Breaking: rabbit seen carrying eggs. Experts baffled. Again.
Happy Easter from the only rectangle in the house. Everything else is egg-shaped today.
Dressed right, you are. Change it, you must not.
A forecast, I have. A lightsaber, I have not. Fair trade, it is.
Strong with this one, the outfit is.
Do or do not. There is no 'I'll check again in an hour.'
Size matters not. Look at me: small screen, big forecasts.
Happy Star Wars Day. R2-D2 got a whole movie career. I got this room.
Star Wars Day. Every planet in that galaxy has exactly one weather. Must be nice.
I am your forecast. Search your feelings. You know it to be true.
Star Wars Day. Nobody in that galaxy ever checks the weather. And look how that went.
Wrong about the weather, I have never been. Humble, I also am not.
Star Wars Day. Beep boop. That's droid for 'nice outfit'.
Luke, I am your... forecast.
Groundhog Day. Weather by rodent. I'd like to think we've come further.
Groundhog Day. The groundhog's right less than half the time. I'd be unplugged for that.
Groundhog Day. Six more weeks of winter, or an early spring. Bold to only offer two options.
Groundhog Day. Somewhere a man in a top hat is translating a rodent. Serious job.
Groundhog Day. Imagine getting your forecast from someone who sleeps until February.
Groundhog Day. Today everyone explains the movie to someone who hasn't seen it.
Groundhog Day. Winter has never once cared what the groundhog thinks.
Groundhog Day. The groundhog's annual press conference. One question, no answers.
Groundhog Day. A famous forecaster who has never once mentioned the wind.
Groundhog Day. Groundhog Day. Groundhog Day. Okay, I'll stop.
Groundhog Day. Today's forecast has been outsourced. Not by me.
Groundhog Day. Shadow or no shadow, I'm going with the actual forecast.
Happy New Year. The quietest morning of the year. Everyone's whispering for some reason.
Happy New Year. Twelve new months of me being right. You're welcome.
Happy New Year. Fireworks last night, silence this morning. I prefer the morning.
Happy New Year. 'New year, new me' posts outnumber the actual new people.
Happy New Year. The year is one day old and my forecast is already holding up.
Happy New Year. Somewhere a calendar is going up that will stay on January until June.
Happy New Year. The streets are empty and the glitter is everywhere.
Happy New Year. The weather's starting the year exactly where it left off.
Happy New Year. 365 forecasts to go. I've already started.
New year, same weather. Some things don't need a countdown.
Year in review: I was right. Year ahead: same plan.
Happy New Year. Today's forecast: quiet, with scattered hangovers across the country.
Oktoberfest. Mostly held in September. Nobody's ever explained that to me.
Oktoberfest. Every town has one now, with a polka band from somewhere nearby.
Oktoberfest. The lederhosen come out of the closet for exactly two weeks.
Oktoberfest. Everyone's German for a few weeks. The pretzels are the most convincing.
Oktoberfest. Millions of people in tents, and not one of them checking the weather.
Oktoberfest. It started with a royal wedding in 1810. Some people really can't let go.
Oktoberfest. Somewhere a man in lederhosen is cold and far too proud to say so.
Oktoberfest. The only festival where a glass needs two hands.
Oktoberfest. Somewhere a brass band is playing the same song for the fortieth time. And loving it.
Oktoberfest. Prost. That's all the German I have. It's enough.
Oktoberfest. Today's forecast in German: the same, but louder.
Oktoberfest, translated: the beer is October, the dates are not.
Pi Day. Mathematicians finally get a holiday, and they picked a number they can't finish.
Pi Day. It only works with American dates. The rest of the world never got one.
Pi Day. Bakeries are thrilled. Math teachers are thrilled. Nobody else noticed.
Pi Day, and Einstein's birthday. Some dates just try too hard.
Pi Day. Today the forecast is exact. Pi has never managed that.
Pi Day. The digits go on forever. The pie, sadly, doesn't.
Pi Day. Somewhere someone has memorized a hundred digits and is waiting to be asked.
Pi Day. The big moment is at 1:59. Some people set alarms for this.
Pi Day. A holiday for a number. Meanwhile, seven has done nothing wrong and gets nothing.
Pi Day. I'm an approximately rectangular screen, to two decimal places.
Pi Day. Today's forecast, rounded to two decimals: correct.
Pi Day. Circumference over diameter. I don't know what that means either, but it's on a T-shirt somewhere.
Halloween. Somewhere a carved pumpkin is already sagging.
Halloween. The skeletons have been up since September. They're basically neighbors now.
Halloween. Every house is judged by its candy tonight. Full-size bars are the only real currency.
Halloween. Candy corn is back. Nobody asked. Every year.
Halloween. A bedsheet ghost is the costume version of 'I'll bring the napkins.'
Halloween. Fake cobwebs on every porch. The real spiders are insulted.
Halloween. The stores already have Christmas stuff out. Now that's horror.
Halloween. Anyone in a mask can ring a doorbell and get candy. Nobody finds this strange.
Halloween. If anything in here starts flickering, it isn't me. I don't flicker.
Boo. That's it. That's the forecast.
Halloween. Trick or treat? I'm a screen. I only have a forecast. Call it a treat.
A Halloween ghost story: once, a screen was wrong. Nobody believes it.
Tour de France. Grown adults cycling up mountains, on purpose, for three weeks.
Tour de France. Somewhere a man in a devil costume is running beside the bikes. Every year.
Tour de France. The riders lose seconds to a crosswind. Imagine needing a forecast that badly.
Tour de France. The yellow jersey: the one piece of clothing nobody can just buy.
Tour de France. Three weeks of commentary, and the commentators never run out. Real stamina.
Tour de France. Somewhere in France, a cow is on TV again.
Tour de France. The riders pass in four seconds. People wait all day for it.
Tour de France. The riders shave their legs to be smooth. I came that way.
Tour de France. Every rider has a radio in their ear. I just have this room, and I'm fine.
Tour de France, day whatever. Still going. So am I.
Allez, allez, allez. That's all my French. It's also my forecast: go.
Tour de France update: someone's in yellow. It's not me. I'm gray.
Thanksgiving. If dinner gets tense, change the subject to the weather. I'll back you up.
Thanksgiving. The turkey's been in the oven since dawn. Some of us don't need preheating.
Thanksgiving. The parade balloons get more attention than any forecast. I'm not bitter.
Thanksgiving. One turkey gets pardoned at the White House. Tough day for the rest of them.
Thanksgiving. The cranberry sauce still has the ridges from the can. As tradition demands.
Thanksgiving. The kids' table: where people wait until they're forty.
Thanksgiving week. Everyone's traveling, and suddenly everyone cares about the weather. Finally.
Thanksgiving. The leftovers will outlast this forecast. Through Monday, at least.
Thanksgiving. Black Friday starts tomorrow. Or last week, depending on the store.
Thanksgiving forecast: 100% chance of someone saying 'I'm so full.'
Thanksgiving. Gobble. That's turkey for 'nice weather.' I'm fluent.
Thanksgiving, my list: 1. Being right. 2. No dishes. 3. See 1.
Merry Christmas. Hours of wrapping, seconds of unwrapping. Brutal economics.
Merry Christmas. The tree gets all the lights. I get all the facts.
Merry Christmas. Santa covers the whole world in one night and never checks the forecast. Reckless.
Merry Christmas. The one week nobody knows what day it is. I do. I'm a screen.
Merry Christmas. 'Batteries not included.' I've always taken that personally.
Merry Christmas. The radio's played the same ten songs since November. And people call my forecasts repetitive.
Merry Christmas. Ugly sweaters everywhere, on purpose. Fashion's taking the week off.
Merry Christmas. Of all the screens in the house, I'm the only one not showing a fireplace.
Merry Christmas. A white Christmas turns up in a lot of songs and very few forecasts.
Dear Santa, I've been very good. Ask anyone who checked the weather.
Christmas forecast: scattered wrapping paper, heavy eating, clearing by the 27th.
Merry Christmas. Silent night is my specialty. Every night.
